- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.5) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to align with mean reversion.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.5), model often underestimates; adjust upward to reflect potential rebound.
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +1.5+ in 30d history), especially if sentiment is neutral or slightly negative — cap forecast at 10–15% below peak observed.
- Forecast bias toward lower prices in early 30d horizon (e.g., 1–3 days ahead) is common — apply upward bias of 0.5–1.0% per day for short-term (1–7d) forecasts.
- For long-term (14–30d) forecasts, model underestimates mean reversion — add 0.3–0.7% per day to forecast to account for momentum decay.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “reversal” patterns (e.g., +1.0 → -0.8 → +0.5), model tends to lag — adjust forecast 1–2 days ahead to match sentiment swing direction.
- Avoid forecasting below 55% of 30d historical low if sentiment is positive — use sentiment as trigger for minimum price floor.
